summary.intent: Execute Phase 23 (rust-sdk-extraction) of the cipher-box project, extracting crypto, core, api-client, fuse, and sdk functionality into a Cargo workspace with separate crates.
summary.outcome: Waves 1 and 2 completed successfully (cipherbox-crypto, cipherbox-core, cipherbox-api-client + test vectors). Wave 3 (cipherbox-fuse, cipherbox-sdk) was interrupted mid-execution by a usage limit reset, leaving partial uncommitted work in both crate directories. A retry was initiated but the transcript ends before confirming completion.

repo: Phase 23 lives on branch feat/phase-23-rust-sdk-extraction and follows a 4-wave dependency order: crypto → core+api-client → fuse+sdk → desktop-shell+CI
Cargo workspace root was introduced in this phase; prior to Phase 23 all crypto lived in desktop app local modules
162 existing desktop tests survived the cipherbox-core extraction, indicating the desktop app maintained backward compatibility
Cross-language test vectors (9 JSON files, 5 parity tests) were added in plan 23-03 to validate Rust/TypeScript parity

workflow: GSD wave-based execution resumes gracefully: re-running execute-phase re-spawns only incomplete plans (those without SUMMARY.md)
Usage limit interruptions mid-agent leave uncommitted partial work in the working tree — spot-checks (SUMMARY.md + git log) are the right way to detect this state
Pre-wave dependency checks (gsd-tools verify key-links) returned no key-links for Wave 3 plans, so no blocking cross-plan wiring gaps were detected

friction: Usage limit hit mid-Wave 3, interrupting both parallel agents before they could commit or create SUMMARY.md files
Partial uncommitted crate directories left in working tree after interruption required manual spot-checking before retry
